description: Registered elevator devices in New York City, as provided by the NYC Department of Buildings in response to a September 2015 FOIL request. The data was received in November 2015 and covers ~76k devices. Includes elevators, escalators, dumbwaiters, and other vertical transportation devices.

columns.name: dv_device_number
columns.description: Unique device number assigned by the NYC Department of Buildings. Can be used to look up a device on the DOB Building Information Search (Field 26).

columns.name: device_status
columns.description: Single-letter code for the device's registration status.

columns.name: bin
columns.description: Building Identification Number, a unique identifier assigned by the NYC Department of Buildings to each building. More reliable than street address for geolocation.

columns.name: tax_block
columns.description: Tax block number within the borough, part of the BBL.

columns.name: tax_lot
columns.description: Tax lot number within the block, part of the BBL. Stored as a string because some lots have letter suffixes (e.g. 7501T).

columns.name: house_number
columns.description: Street number portion of the filed at address.

columns.name: street_name
columns.description: Street name portion of the filed at address.

columns.name: zip_code
columns.description: Five-digit ZIP code for the filed at address.

columns.name: borough
columns.description: NYC borough where the device is located. A small number of rows have this field blank.

columns.name: device_type
columns.description: Type of elevator device.

columns.name: dv_lastper_insp_date
columns.description: Date of the last periodic inspection by the NYC Department of Buildings. May be missing if the device has never been inspected. Because the data is from late 2015, these dates may no longer be current.

columns.name: dv_lastper_insp_disp
columns.description: Disposition code from the last periodic inspection. Missing if no inspection on record. II appears 17 times and its meaning is not documented anywhere; 18 rows using codes seen fewer than 10 times were treated as data entry errors and set to missing.

columns.name: dv_approval_date
columns.description: Date the device was approved. Typically reflects when the device was first registered or last had a major approval action.

columns.name: dv_manufacturer
columns.description: Name of the device manufacturer as entered by the filer. Free-text with many inconsistencies (e.g. OTIS and OTIS ELEV CO are the same company). Over 2,000 unique values. Some entries like HOUSING AUTHORITY or PRIVATE RESIDENCE describe ownership rather than manufacturer.

columns.name: dv_travel_distance
columns.description: Vertical travel distance of the device in feet. Often omitted (~62% missing). Parsed from highly inconsistent raw strings. See travel-distance.qmd for details.

columns.name: dv_speed_fpm
columns.description: Speed of the device in feet per minute. Common values include 50, 100, 200, 350. Converted from string by extracting leading numeric values (e.g. 95UP -> 95). 16 unparseable entries (e.g. ----, VAR, EX) were set to missing.

columns.name: dv_capacity_lbs
columns.description: Weight capacity of the device in pounds. Common values include 2500, 3000, 3500 for passenger elevators. Converted from string by fixing O/o -> 0, removing commas, and extracting leading numeric values. 6 unparseable entries (e.g. ESC, NIUD) were set to missing.

columns.name: dv_car_buffer_type
columns.description: Type of car buffer. Often missing, particularly for non-elevator devices. R (41 rows) is an inferred label. 42 rows using digits or codes seen fewer than 10 times were treated as data entry errors and set to missing.

columns.name: dv_governor_type
columns.description: Type of speed governor. Often missing for non-elevator devices. I and O are inferred labels; B, G, and V are used often enough to be real codes but their meanings are not documented anywhere. 29 rows using digits or codes seen fewer than 10 times were treated as data entry errors and set to missing.

columns.name: dv_machine_type
columns.description: Type of hoisting machine. Missing for some devices. OD (652 rows, concentrated in dumbwaiters and freight elevators), D, H, and RP are inferred labels; A (243 rows), B (224 rows), LT, and WT are undocumented. 23 rows using codes seen fewer than 10 times were treated as data entry errors and set to missing.

columns.name: dv_safety_type
columns.description: Type of safety device. Missing for roughly half of all devices. W, N, and O are inferred labels; the remaining codes are undocumented, though B and C may correspond to the ASME Type B and Type C safety classes. 53 rows using digits, punctuation, or codes seen fewer than 10 times were treated as data entry errors and set to missing.

columns.name: dv_mode_operation
columns.description: Mode of operation. Missing for some devices. N is an inferred label; R (42 rows) and K (11 rows, all on escalators) are undocumented. 59 rows using digits or codes seen fewer than 10 times were treated as data entry errors and set to missing.

columns.name: dv_status_date
columns.description: Date when the device status was last updated.

columns.name: dv_floor_from
columns.description: Lowest floor served by the device. May be an integer (1), a standard letter code (B basement, C cellar, L lobby, G ground, M mezzanine, SB sub-basement, SC sub-cellar), or a comma-separated pair indicating two lobby entry levels (e.g. B,1). See floor.qmd for details.

columns.name: dv_floor_to
columns.description: Highest floor served by the device. Uses the same notation as dv_floor_from. Common letter codes include PH (penthouse), R (roof), T (top), and ST (street). Subject to the same cleaning as dv_floor_from.

columns.name: latitude
columns.description: Approximate latitude of the device's building, obtained by geocoding the BIN, Borough-Block-Lot, or street address via the NYC Geoclient API. Not authoritative; some values may be in error.

columns.name: longitude
columns.description: Approximate longitude of the device's building, obtained by geocoding. Not authoritative; some values may be in error.

glossary.definition: Building Identification Number. A unique numeric identifier assigned to each building by the NYC Department of Buildings.
Borough-Block-Lot. A three-part identifier (borough code, tax block, tax lot) used by NYC to uniquely identify a parcel of land for property tax purposes.
New York City Department of Buildings. The agency responsible for ensuring the safe and lawful use of buildings and properties.
New York City Housing Authority. The public housing authority for NYC, which manages its own elevator inspection program.
A required inspection of elevator devices conducted by the NYC Department of Buildings on a regular cycle (typically annual or biennial depending on device type).
A continuous-loop conveyor with platforms or steps used to transport people between floors. Largely obsolete and rarely installed new.
A freight elevator that opens at sidewalk level, used to move goods between the sidewalk and a building's basement or cellar.
An elevator machine type where the motor directly drives the sheave without a gearbox. Used in high-rise buildings for high speeds and smooth operation.
A speed-limiting safety device on an elevator. If the car exceeds a set speed, the governor triggers the safety mechanism to stop the car.

The address where the elevator application or paperwork was filed with the Department of Buildings. This may differ from the actual physical location of the device. The BIN or Borough-Block-Lot is generally more reliable for geolocation.
A shock-absorbing device at the bottom of the elevator shaft that cushions the car in the event of an overrun. Spring buffers are used for lower speeds; oil buffers for higher speeds.
